subtitle: A Toltec episode as transmitted by Spence

departure.author: Lewis Spence
departure.locator: Chapter II · MEXICAN MYTHOLOGY; Chapter II · MEXICAN MYTHOLOGY, normalized characters 20022-20201
departure.excerpt: On reaching the summit of Mount Poyauhtecatl he slid to the base. Arriving at the sea-shore, he embarked upon a raft of serpents, and was wafted away toward the land of Tlapallan.
departure.note: Verbatim prose from Lewis Spence's early twentieth-century synthesis, not a direct translation of the Indigenous source material he discusses. Preserve its dated, colonial framing.

narrativeBlocks.title: A journey away from Mexico
narrativeBlocks.body: Spence's account describes Quetzalcoatl leaving Mexico, reaching the shore, and departing on a raft of serpents toward Tlapallan.

narrativeBlocks.title: The raft of serpents
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Spence's English prose synthesis (whitespace normalized): “On reaching the summit of Mount Poyauhtecatl he slid to the base. Arriving at the sea-shore, he embarked upon a raft of serpents, and was wafted away toward the land of Tlapallan.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A named transmission
narrativeBlocks.body: Spence says the legends are taken from Sahagun's Historia General de Nueva España and compared with accounts attributed to Ixtlilxochitl.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep the Toltec setting
narrativeBlocks.body: Spence places this in a discussion of Toltec legends and the fall of Tollan. Do not collapse it into a single story shared identically by all Mesoamerican peoples.

narrativeBlocks.title: Departure is not one fixed ending
narrativeBlocks.body: The passage records one written synthesis of a departure tradition. The text itself notes parallels and comparison, not a single uncontested version.
